title: At the dining hall, night
text: “One way or another, you experience all sorts of things.”

Whatever the topic, Arc had a way of talking about things on an absolutely enormous scale, I say. With a faint smile, Arc dropped a Lucor fruit into a glass of wine and began sipping it little by little.
“Well, that cat over there used to have a pretty troublesome personality too, back in the day~”

“Old is right. And get this—thanks to a bit of liquid courage, the girl in question literally tackled the boy to the ground. Turns out the boy was dense enough about, well, various things, that it took something that drastic to get through to him. Ah, though the reason was that the girl had declared she hated men in the first place.”
Arc laughed while saying this. Ah, yes—nothing pairs better with a drink than gossiping about someone else’s love life, I say.
“The Lucor fruit’s that old… it’s been around since before this world even existed.”
“That old, huh. This thing.”
“Yup.”
Arc nodded.
“Sadeena-neesan. It seems Arc and the others can’t actually get drunk, so please go easy.”
“Ohh, fine, fine~”
Scolded by Big Sister, Older Sister seemed to back down.
“But you’re still keeping me company with drinks, Big Sister~!”
“Between the three of us, we could probably drink her under the table pretty quick.”
“Isn’t moderation important here?”
“So much energy~”

Father and the others ended up joining as Older Sister’s drinking companions. By the time they’d finally drunk Older Sister into unconsciousness, everyone had finished eating and started drifting off to bed in their own ways. For some, it was bath time.
“So where are you two sleeping?”
“We’re not really built for sleep, so… if it’s just resting you mean, anywhere’s fine?”
“My sleep cycle means I’m not turning in yet either, so don’t worry about me~”
Arc and the others each answered Father’s question in turn. Not sleeping at all? Really?
“That won’t do… anyway, for the bird one, the Filolial barn’s fine, right?”
“Ahh, how cruel~ Lumping me in with them~ Those kids won’t get any sleep with me around.”
Oh ho, seemed Ho-kun was being considerate, worried that Filolial-sama would get too nervous around him to sleep.
“Ho-kun, Filolial-sama, you’re welcome to come stay at my place, I say.”
“Mokkun!?”
“Mo-chan!?”
“Motoyasu-san!?”
Oh? Kou and the others, who’d been keeping a respectful distance out of deference to Ho-kun, suddenly looked shocked.
“Since you’re troubled about where to sleep, welcoming you in is my duty, I say.”
“No… I don’t want it to be your duty. And could you stop treating me like a Filolial? I keep telling you, I’m a phoenix.”
Ho-kun was so cold, I say. Even so, I would love that Filolial-sama regardless, I say.
“Could you please stop with that burning gaze… anyway, it’s fine! I’m great at building nests!”
“You should probably stop him. This bird will literally bring in nesting materials from who-knows-where and build something so absurdly huge it counts as a house.”
“……Either way, we’ve got an empty guest house, so rest there. Sounds like a hassle otherwise. Just don’t make a mess.”
“As if I’d make a mess.”
“Right~ So that’s that, Motoyasu-kun, no need to worry about it.”
Ahh, how unfortunate, I say. I’d wanted to catch a bit more of Ho-kun’s scent.
“Hmm… goosebumps.”
“You’re literally a bird.”
“You’ve been a bird from the start, so that’s a given.”
Father and Arc pointed this out in perfect unison. And so Father led Ho-kun and the others off to the empty house.
Eventually… night deepened. Once it had grown quite late, I headed out for my nightly stroll, and noticed light spilling from the dining hall. Looking inside, I found Arc and Ho-kun there.
“Oh? What are you two doing at this hour, I say?”

“Ah, Motoyasu-kun. Nothing much, just bored, so I’m hanging around the dining hall. Seems like the village kids are out and about at night too, just like you, so I figured I’d chat with whoever showed up. If you ask that cat over there, she’ll get you some milk.”
“Naofumi-kun gave us permission~”

Arc had spread out what looked like some kind of tools across the dining table and was fiddling with them, clinking and clacking away. What could this be about? Arc reached out, grasped what looked like a necklace, and gave it a little shake. Suddenly, a ring appeared in midair. Something drifted out of the ring—not quite a will-o’-the-wisp, not quite a firefly—and the ring itself dropped into Arc’s hand. Arc gave the ring a click, and a part came loose. Using a towel, Arc cleaned the piece, examined a gem-like component, and held a hand over it, doing something or other. This was craftsmanship, I say. It looked just like the accessory-making Father did! No doubt some task related to god-hunting or the like. It even looked somewhat like a ring version of the spear I carried, though surely that was just my imagination. Once the tinkering with the ring seemed finished, Arc picked up the necklace again and gave it another shake. Light poured into the ring and then vanished. But as if taking its turn, something similar appeared next—a bell with a gem attached. Arc disassembled that in the same way and continued the cleaning work.
“So, Motoyasu-kun. Something you need?”
“Just a stroll, I say. I’m checking to see if any Filolial-sama are having trouble sleeping, I say.”
“Heh, diligent of you.”
“Naturally, I say. Ho-kun, are you two really certain you don’t need sleep? Shall I run a health check, I say?”
“Yup. Just how my lifestyle works. I still don’t need to sleep yet.”
“I never sleep to begin with.”

What impressive individuals, not needing sleep at all. As for Arc, apparently some kind of superior to the dragons… now that I thought of it, I recalled hearing legends back in Japan about dragons that never slept. No doubt this was that same sort of nature at work.
“Ho-kun, if you’re sleepy but can’t sleep, I could stay with you until I fall asleep myself… if you’d like, I say?”
“No, that’s not it at all. No need to go out of your way like that.”
“Ha, you’re a funny one, Motoyasu-kun. Getting a bird to play straight man like that.”
“So cruel~”
“Oh right, Naofumi-kun stopped by earlier too. Said he had prep work for tomorrow. Raphtalia-chan and someone named Raph-chan came to fetch him, and he went home rather reluctantly.”
Father was one to stay up fairly late himself, I say. Big Sister must have called out to him and brought him home.
“Even if you say you don’t sleep, overexerting yourselves can’t be good for your health, I say. I’d like you both to rest when you have the chance.”

These were people whose very profession was hunting down beings who falsely claimed godhood, much like the Crimson Swine herself. It was exactly at times like these that I wished they’d take a proper rest.
“I’ll take the sentiment.”
“You worry about us, don’t you, Motoyasu-kun. Thank you.”
At the sound of that voice and the sight of that expression as Arc looked up and answered with a smile, I felt, once again, that same sharp, nagging sensation catch at me, I say.
“Well then, if you’ll excuse me, I say.”
And with that, I finished my walk and retired to my room for the night.

A few days later, one morning. Arc and Ho-kun had settled well into the village by now, I say. They watched over the lively daily life of the village with clear enjoyment. Occasionally, they even stood in for Father.
“Hmph! Haaaah!”

A loud shout from Ren rang out during his morning training. Since it was quite noisy, I went to see what was going on. Most likely he was training alongside Éclair and the villagers as part of his morning regimen. Sure enough, there were Ren, Éclair, Black Thunder, and Arc and Ho-kun as well. The old woman and Stalker Pig were nowhere to be seen.
“More! Give me more!”

Ren seemed to be sparring against Arc. Yet for some reason, a huge number of glowing swords floated in the air around them. Facing him, Arc held a glowing sword. And for whatever reason, Arc was wearing a crown. According to the story, Ren had handed it over and asked Arc to wear it.
“Got it. Here I go, then.”

Arc made a throwing motion with the glowing sword, and the countless glowing swords floating around them shot toward Ren from every direction. Like the Hundred Swords technique Ren himself used, an innumerable rain of blades came pouring down.
“Ooooooooh!”
Ren deflected the glowing swords with Sword 0 and charged straight at Arc.
